proofs.text: Call `write_record()` with a record whose commit is `4f1c2ab9e1d4e8c9b5f2a7d3c6e0b8a1d9f4c2e7` and a runner email `ada@example.com`; verify the returned path is `.purlin/records/greeting/<timestamp>-4f1c2ab-ada.json`, that the reader parses the four parts back out of it, that `os_name="windows"` adds the `-windows` tail and sets the file's `os` field to `windows`, and that the dict the caller handed over is not mutated

rule_text: A record is written to `.purlin/records/<feature>/<timestamp>-<commit7>-<runner>[-<os>].json`, where `<runner>` is `ci` or the local part of the committer's email, and the `runner`, `os` and `timestamp` fields inside the file are set to match the name rather than left as the caller handed them over

tests.body:
def test_the_file_name_carries_the_run(project):
    when = datetime(2026, 9, 13, 12, 0, 0)
    name = records_module.record_filename(
        '4f1c2ab9e1d4e8c9b5f2a7d3c6e0b8a1', 'ada@example.com', 'linux', when)
    assert name == '20260913T120000Z-4f1c2ab-ada-linux.json'
    parts = reader.record_name_parts(name)
    assert parts == ('20260913T120000Z', '4f1c2ab', 'ada', 'linux')
tests.name: test_the_file_name_carries_the_run
